title: The End of the Internet
author: Ben Thompson
description: The old Internet, where anyone could host a server is over, but it's just the final blow in an ending that has been coming for years. The future, though, is brighter than it appears.
summary: Listen to this post : Log in to listen It was the summer of 2003, just weeks before I was set to move to Taiwan, that I decided to create a blog to document my journey. I had, at that point, had a GeoCities site, a Blogspot site, a site I built in Microsoft FrontPage and hosted…somewhere, so this was my fourth swing at the blog thing (it was the seventh that ended up being Stratechery).
takeaways: Right there was the exact loyalty that Klein fears has been lost… I am, of course, acutely aware that there is a tradeoff when it comes to the subscription business model: by making something scarce, and worth paying for, you are by definition limiting your number of readers.
For many years I rued the fact I wasn’t one of those early bloggers; a decade later, however, I realized that I was actually just in time for a much more sustainable business model: subscriptions.
I wrote in 2015’s Blogging’s Bright Future : It turns out, though, that there are more business models than simply advertising, as Sullivan himself sought to show.
